## Why
The [current Scout step](https://github.com/grove/gapline/blob/main/gapline-audit/SKILL.md) deliberately selects a few consequential leads, but it provides limited help allocating a small inspection budget across a large or unfamiliar codebase. Better candidate selection may improve practical value without requiring more finding categories or a new tool.

**Evidence gate:** use the results of [real-host validation](https://github.com/grove/gapline/issues/4) and [matched effectiveness evaluation](https://github.com/grove/gapline/issues/5) to choose failure cases worth addressing; do not assume more scouting rules improve audits.

## Proposed approach
- Study where current Scout exploration wastes effort or overlooks meaningful risk, based on retained traces or independently reviewed examples.
- Design a **short optional decision aid** emphasizing consequences, user priorities, public promises, reachable boundaries, uncertainty, and evidence availability. Context-specific examples (authentication, payment retries, state persistence) are illustrative, not a mandatory scan list.
- Preserve narrow focus versus sampled-survey modes, read-only constraints, the default three-lead ceiling, an explicit stop budget, and the option to return no findings.
- Compare the guidance with existing Gapline Scout on matched realistic questions, including low-risk code and a valid unusual design. Assess whether chosen probes and confirmed developer value improve at similar cost.
- Revert or simplify guidance if it primarily increases token use, superficial warnings, or repeated exploration.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Document specific observed shortcomings of present scouting; distinguish observations from hypotheses.
- [ ] Proposed guidance changes **prioritization**, not the set of required lenses or reported findings.
- [ ] Matched trials show whether the new strategy improves useful leads / avoids wasted probes; include contrary and inconclusive results.
- [ ] No new required parser, runtime, language-specific tool, or host capability; optional subagent behavior remains bounded.
- [ ] Update the installed skill/reference and relevant evaluation examples **only if** the observed tradeoff justifies it.

## Out of scope
Exhaustive architecture maps, mandatory threat-model checklists, code-quality scoring, automatic execution, or a full repository index.

## Scouting lesson from pg-trickle: scoped prompts were a major confounder

Two read-only user runs targeted a large Rust/PostgreSQL project ([pg-trickle @ `066bd5dcdfca`](https://github.com/trickle-labs/pg-trickle/commit/066bd5dcdfca8ad9ee3de9cf012a52d2774ba5dc)), each producing at most three leads ([issues #1158–#1163](https://github.com/trickle-labs/pg-trickle/issues?q=is%3Aissue+is%3Aopen+1158+1159+1160+1161+1162+1163); individual issue links below).

**Observed:** The first prompt *already named* CDC, refresh, frontiers, WAL handoff, crash recovery, and relevant source directories. Its output pursued exactly those consequential boundaries: [late commit/frontier](https://github.com/trickle-labs/pg-trickle/issues/1158), [fallback/receipt](https://github.com/trickle-labs/pg-trickle/issues/1159), [FULL/frontier alignment](https://github.com/trickle-labs/pg-trickle/issues/1160). The second prompt *already named* README, capability manifest, DVM matrix and roadmap; its output focused on [clock freshness](https://github.com/trickle-labs/pg-trickle/issues/1161), [IMMEDIATE docs](https://github.com/trickle-labs/pg-trickle/issues/1162), [recursive docs](https://github.com/trickle-labs/pg-trickle/issues/1163). We have no retained detailed exploration trace or matched broad question to show how much of this selection came from Gapline's Scout.

**Potentially valuable decision aid (hypothesis, not yet a skill-change justification):** prefer an explicit user promise/contract and a reachable interaction boundary (e.g., committed-change durability through multiple CDC modes, or support claims versus effective execution) over a broad inventory of stylistic smells. For known historical fixes, check whether equivalent **entry points** inherit the safeguard: [pg-trickle #536](https://github.com/trickle-labs/pg-trickle/issues/536) addressed scheduler visibility, whereas [new #1158](https://github.com/trickle-labs/pg-trickle/issues/1158) raises a manual-path hypothesis.

**Negative/uncertain evidence:** We cannot claim Scout uncovered these risks unprompted or at acceptable marginal cost; time and token budgets were not controlled. Both outputs hit the three-finding ceiling, so a future clean/false-lead control is important to guard against quota-driven conclusions. We have no evidence that a new checklist would do better.

**Suggested test for this issue:** compare current Scout with a *short optional consequence-and-boundary selection heuristic* on several matched, unfamiliar questions; include (a) high-stakes cross-component risk, (b) valid design that looks suspicious, and (c) no actionable risk. Review **probe selection, supported value, missed risks, refutations and cost**, not number of issues. Keep the three-lead ceiling and read-only behavior.

title: [P1] Improve risk-guided scouting without turning Gapline into a checklist
